title: LLM-Guided Communication for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
claim: An LLM designs a communication protocol, then iteratively refines it through criterion-based feedback so all agents recover the state accurately and uniformly.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, LLM hub in center with stacked refinement steps
description: Three dashed-outline panels read left to right. The left panel gives the task goal: three robot agents need to know a target star's position. Below it is a Communication Design box with a small diagram of robots exchanging messages m1 = f_c(o3) and m2 = f_c(o3), with red question-mark and green exclamation bubbles showing who knows the star's location. The center holds a brain-shaped LLM icon. A speech bubble above asks how to improve the protocol so agents share the same knowledge. A feedback box below pairs a magnifier-and-chart icon with a checklist icon. Large gray arrows lead to the right panel, Criterion-based Refinement Process. It stacks an initial protocol box, a blue Step 1 Recovery Enhancement box and a pink Step 2 Imbalance Mitigation box. Red feedback labels and down arrows link them, and Python code-update icons sit at the right. Yellow, blue and pink color-code the stages.
caption: Protocol refinement in LMAC. Given natural-language descriptions of the task goal and the state and observation dimensions, the LLM designs an initial communication protocol to support accurate state reconstruction (star position in the figure). The protocol is then refined via criterion-based two-step feedback to make reconstruction more accurate and uniform by sharing missing local information: Step 1 improves each agent’s state reconstruction accuracy, and Step 2 reduces information gaps across agents.
abstract: Communication is a key component in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for mitigating partial observability, yet prior approaches often rely on inefficient information exchange or fail to transmit sufficient state information. To address this, we propose LLM-driven Multi-Agent Communication (LMAC), which leverages an LLM's reasoning capability to design a communication protocol that enables all agents to reconstruct the underlying state as accurately and uniformly as possible. LMAC iteratively refines the protocol using an explicit state-awareness criterion, improving state recovery while narrowing differences in agents' knowledge. Experiments on diverse MARL benchmarks show that LMAC improves state reconstruction across agents and yields substantial performance gains over prior communication baselines.
